requirements.statement: The sign-in page offers a “Forgot password?” link that starts a password reset request.
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer is on the sign-in page, when they select “Forgot password?”, then a password reset request starts.

requirements.statement: A password reset request receives the same response whether or not the account exists.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise equivalent reset requests for an existing and a nonexistent account, when each request is submitted, then their responses are identical.

requirements.statement: Password reset requests are limited to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given five reset requests have been allowed for an account within an hour, when another is attempted for that account within the same hour, then no sixth reset request is allowed.

requirements.statement: A reset link can complete at most one password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reset link has already been used successfully, when it is used again, then it does not complete another reset.

requirements.statement: A reset link expires 30 minutes after issuance.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reset link was issued, when its use is attempted 30 minutes or more after issuance, then it cannot complete a reset.

requirements.statement: A customer can complete a password reset using a valid reset link.
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer has an unused, unexpired reset link, when the customer completes the reset, then the account password is reset.

requirements.statement: Completing a password reset signs the account out of every active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account has active sessions, when its password reset completes successfully, then all those sessions are signed out.

requirements.statement: The account owner is notified after every successful password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account's password reset succeeds, when the reset has completed, then the account owner is notified after that reset.
